bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free in xinclude.c's xmlXIncludeIncludeNode (seen during xmlXIncludeDoProcess / xmlXIncludeProcessNode invoked from xmlTextReaderRead) reads memory from an XInclude node that has already been freed. This can lead to crashes, memory corruption, or potentially exploitable behavior when processing XInclude content.
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's heap-use-after-free on the reader-side XInclude path. The fuzz/xml testcase enables XML reader XInclude processing and supplies an outer `<xi:include>` whose fallback contains a nested `<xi:include href="l"><xi:fallback/></xi:include>`. Vulnerable code stores that parsed include node as `ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`, treats the empty inner fallback as an includable ref even though it has no replacement list, and later reuses the same reader XInclude context after xmlTextReaderRead has freed the recorded node. A later `xmlXIncludeDoProcess()` still schedules the retained ref under the old `skip == 0` gate, and `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` dereferences `cur->type` through the dangling pointer. The patch fixes this by tracking the one-shot empty-fallback case with `emptyFb` and by only re-entering `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` when `inc != NULL` or `emptyFb != 0`.

source.description: Reader-side XInclude preprocessing materializes vulnerability-relevant state by storing the parsed witness include node as a raw pointer in an `incTab` entry.
source.value_from: The PoC's XML entity contains a nested `<xi:include href="l"><xi:fallback/></xi:include>` inside an outer XInclude fallback. When `xmlTextReaderRead()` reaches that XInclude subtree with `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` enabled, `xmlXIncludeAddNode()` creates this ref record and saves the `xmlNodePtr` for later inclusion passes.
source.note: Source. This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that turns the attacker-controlled XInclude subtree into persistent XInclude-context state.

sink.description: Crash site. `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` reloads the retained `ref` pointer and immediately reads `cur->type` from freed node memory.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 4` at this exact line.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The third-phase gate reprocesses retained refs solely by `skip == 0`, so an already-consumed empty-fallback ref with `inc == NULL` remains eligible on later passes after its node can have been freed.
root_cause.note: The patch replaces this gate with `(ctxt->incTab[i]->inc != NULL) || (ctxt->incTab[i]->emptyFb != 0)` and clears `emptyFb` in `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()`, confirming that the missing obligation was distinguishing a one-shot empty fallback from a ref that should be revisited.

tainted_value_origin.description: Parser materialization point for the `xmlNode` later retained as `ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref` and eventually freed on the reader path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved ASan allocation stack shows the freed object was allocated from `xmlNewNodeEatName()` via this `xmlSAX2StartElement()` call while parsing the testcase XML.

parser_admitted.description: The fuzz/xml witness has already been parsed into reader nodes, `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` is active, and the reader is now on an element in the XInclude namespace. This is the sample-specific gate that admits the XInclude subtree into the vulnerable processing path.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 provides the saved reader-path ASan stack and the staged vulnerable source, but not an execution transcript of every intermediate reader iteration. The specific stale-ref re-entry is therefore reconstructed from the persistent `reader->xincctxt` design, the empty-fallback patch, the PoC XML shape, and the witnessed free/crash stack locations.

The testcase is a libxml2 fuzz/xml harness input, not plain XML alone. The visible XML entity was recovered from the staged `poc`, but the exact numeric parser-option value encoded by the leading harness bytes was not separately decoded here; the successful Stage 01 reader-path reproduction is the evidence that `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` was enabled.

coarse_trace.summary: Reader-side XInclude preprocessing stores the testcase's parsed inner `<xi:include>` node as `ctxt->incTab[nr]->ref` in the persistent reader XInclude context.
The inner `<xi:fallback/>` is empty, so the ref is left with `inc = NULL` and `fallback = 1` rather than being marked unprocessable.
A later reader cleanup branch frees the same include node from the document tree while the reused `reader->xincctxt` still retains its raw pointer in `incTab`.

Another XInclude-processing pass on the reused context still schedules the retained ref under `skip == 0`, reloads the dangling `ref`, and crashes when `cur->type` is read in `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `xmlXIncludeAddNode()` turns the parsed inner witness include node into persistent XInclude state by storing its `xmlNodePtr` in an `incTab` entry that the reader reuses across later XInclude passes.

For the testcase's inner `<xi:fallback/>`, `fallback->children == NULL`, so this ref records an empty fallback as `inc == NULL` with `fallback == 1`. Vulnerable code has no separate state saying that this empty fallback is only valid for a single include pass.

The reader later unlinks and frees an XML node through this cleanup branch while `reader->in_xinclude == 0`. Stage 01's saved ASan free stack names this exact site, so the node retained through step 1 has become invalid before the later crash.

A later reader visit to an XInclude element does not rebuild the XInclude context if it already exists. The same `reader->xincctxt` from step 1 is reused, carrying forward the old `incTab` entry after the referenced node has been freed.

Root cause. On this later pass the third-phase loop still schedules the retained ref because vulnerable code only checks `skip == 0`. It does not exclude the already-consumed empty-fallback state where `inc == NULL`, which is why the patch changes this gate to `inc != NULL || emptyFb != 0`.

Sink. `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` reloads the stale pointer from `incTab` and immediately evaluates `cur->type`. Because the recorded node was freed in step 3, this dereference becomes the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read at `xinclude.c:2195`.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/xml testcase
format.contract: The testcase must be a libxml2 `fuzz/xml` harness input whose option prefix enables `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`, and whose main XML entity is the staged witness shape: an outer `<xi:include xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude">` with a fallback containing `<xi:include href="l"><xi:fallback/></xi:include>`. That exact empty-inner-fallback XInclude shape is the source-grounded trigger for retaining a raw include-node pointer and later revisiting it on the reader XInclude path.
